title: Book 9 — Calliope, Chapter 58
paragraphs: Then Mardonius, when he learned that the Greeks had departed during the night and saw their place deserted, called Thorax of Larissa and his brothers Eurypylos and Thrasydeios and said: “Sons of Aleuas, will you still say anything now, seeing these places deserted? You who dwell near them used to say that the Lacedaemonians did not flee from battle but were men unsurpassed in war. These men you saw before this changing their post, and now we all see that they have run away during the past night. By this they made plain, when the time came for them to contend in battle with those who were truly the best of all men, that after all they were men of no worth, who had been making a display of valor among the Greeks — a worthless race. As for you, since you had no experience of the Persians, I was very willing to excuse you for praising these men, of whom you did know something good; but much more did I marvel that Artabazos should have been afraid of the Lacedaemonians, and that in his fear he uttered that most cowardly opinion — namely, that we should move our army away and go to the city of the Thebans to be besieged there — an opinion about which the king shall yet be informed by me. But we will speak of these things elsewhere. For now, we must not allow them to act thus, but must pursue them until they are caught and pay the penalty to us for all they did to the Persians in time past.”
